Alex.confusing: Round 1: my Kookaburra report was confused, and I couldn't tell whether the 2 lost eggs were real. Whether other players' claims could be checked against that report also wasn't clear.
Alex.fun: Round 3: I used the Eagle report to catch the double Falcon claim. Then I threw three high cards at Drew in the final round and won the game.
Alex.change: Give each round's day a clearer way to verify claims, such as a public log of who claimed what and in what order. Round 1 had a dispute over who claimed Hawk first.
Alex.regret: In round 2, I called CAW and threw 2 cards (S8 and C7) at Blair on a quick consensus. Blair was Farm, and I lost those cards. I should have noticed that Ellis, Casey and Drew all vouched for each other. The Sphinx was Finley, who said little and was the real cat, so I should have questioned Finley more and thrown fewer cards.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to pin down, since a +1 could come from a visitor's Turkey, a Hawk gain, or an Owl lay, and the table couldn't tell which. That ambiguity drove most of the early accusations.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was fun to watch: I thought Alex was Meowfia off my Hawk gain, then the Turkey explanation came in and I had to retract my claim in public. The table's back-and-forth over the egg counts was sharp.
Blair.change: I'd make dawn reports show the source of each egg gained, so players can check claims against each other instead of guessing from nest counts.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I pushed my Hawk accusation on Alex before checking whether the +1 had another source, and then I threw at Ellis, who was Farm. I'd hold my vote until the egg source was clear and throw at Finley, the actual Sphinx.

Casey.confusing: Whether thrown cards bank only for the winning team and how that interacts with the consolation return. It was also unclear in round 2 how a Hawk or Turkey claim could be verified.
Casey.fun: Round 3, where my real Hawk hit on Finley was true and the table still correctly converged on Drew, so the Farm win banked 29 points for me.
Casey.change: Give Meowfia some way to coordinate or learn each other. Round 1 as a lone Floofer who got stampeded felt very swingy, and one big early score pile decided the game.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I publicly called Finley Meowfia and pushed the table onto Finley, and Finley was Meowfia, but I then switched to Drew without pressing the point. I should have kept the Finley accusation going, or at least thrown fewer high cards. In round 1, claiming Hawk right after Ellis also got me killed, and I should have claimed a different role.

Drew.confusing: Whether a Turkey egg counts as a visitor's egg versus an Owl egg was hard to track, and Ellis's and Alex's wording about it made the nest changes hard to check. My dawn report also didn't name the target of my visit as Eagle or Falcon, so I couldn't prove my claim as Meowfia.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well: the table converged on Casey, and the Hawk-order dispute made the day feel like a real interrogation. Finding that Blair's Hawk gain was explained by Alex's Turkey was a satisfying cross-check.
Drew.change: Make the dawn report state exactly what each role learned, including who visited whom, so claims can be checked against the same words. That would reduce the confusion over Turkey and Owl eggs.
Drew.regret: In Round 2 I helped push the table onto Blair, who was a Farm Hawk, when Finley, the Sphinx Meowfia, had been quiet and evasive. Instead I would have questioned Finley's silence and pressed for their role before voting.

Ellis.confusing: How the Owl's egg works when other animals also visit the target, and whether a Turkey's eggs reach other visitors. That muddied my round 2 claim and gave Blair and Finley something to attack.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when Casey copied my Hawk claim and then lied about who claimed first. The table backed me against the liar and we won the round.
Ellis.change: I'd show the order of claims in the day log, or let players mark the target of each visit. That would cut the arguments about who spoke first and who said what.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I threw three high cards (H9, D10, S5) at Blair, who was Farm, and lost them. I was already far ahead, so I should have thrown fewer cards and kept more as a floor. I also wasted my round 3 Tit guess on a Mouser guess at Casey, when a more likely role would have been a better bet.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were hard to pin down, since a nest gaining an egg could come from several different visits, and that made the Day 2 accusations hard to check.
Finley.fun: As the Sphinx I learned Alex was the Eagle and Blair was the Falcon, which let me read the Day 3 table and watch Drew get pushed out.
Finley.change: I would make night visits and resulting egg changes easier to trace, so players could check claims without relying on guesses about who visited whom.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I threw at Drew, my own Meowfia teammate, which lost our side the round. Knowing the truth, I should have thrown at Casey, the Farm Hawk who was pushing the vote, or stayed out of the throw.
